articles.title: South Africa v Australia: second men’s cricket Test, day two – live
articles.summary: Updates as the Proteas host Australia at St George’s Park. Start to play in Gqeberha delayed by rain. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. The rain radar that I can find doesn’t look promising either.
body: “Fast bowlers don’t eat as many pies or neck as many beers as they used to back in the day, so the role of the spinner to hold up an end is diminished these days,” suggests David Blackah. “Also drop in pitches don’t take turn until days 4 & 5 and it’s often all over by then.”
There is something to that last bit. Also the fact that teams now bowl about 70 overs a day even when it’s clear and sunny.

Still, I don’t buy the argument that because a game may be shorter, you don’t need a spinner. If it ended in three days without the spinner playing a role, then picking one didn’t hinder your team. And if you think it’ll be a short match but it goes longer, then you have the resource that you need.
I’m told that the St George’s Park band has been playing music for most of the morning, which is hilarious, but even they have stopped now. Tired out. The covers are coming off, though.

articles.title: At Strasbourg, Gio Reyna is starting to gain what had been elusive: momentum
articles.summary: A goal against PSG is proof on the scoresheet of what can be seen on the teamsheet: At long last, Reyna is getting consistent minutes. For an entire four-year cycle, to write about Gio Reyna was to write about his potential – especially the nagging feeling that it was going unfulfilled.
body: Since his emergent 2020-21 season, when he logged nearly 2,000 Bundesliga minutes running alongside Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham, and Jadon Sancho, Reyna finished each of the ensuing five seasons without even cresting 630 league minutes. “Rotational” became a generous descriptor for his role at Nottingham Forest on loan, and then last season with Borussia Mönchengladbach. Still, Gregg Berhalter and Mauricio Pochettino kept involving Reyna with the US squad based on that pesky potential – betting that, on his day, he still had the raw talent to do what few compatriots could.

This year, those days are finally coming with regularity. Since faring well in a contributor’s role at the World Cup, Reyna has moved to France with Strasbourg, and he’s remained first-choice in a youthful squad whose average age of 21.6 more closely resembles a postgrad program than a Ligue 1 roster. Coupled with his newfound status as a two-time World Cup selection, Reyna appears more comfortable as a budding leader than the would-be wunderkind with an unfortunately lengthy injury ledger. Life’s simpler that way.

articles.title: Beer & Blackpool beach was how British players bonded - Pulis
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what Spurs will get from their team-bonding trip to Spain, and how differently managers built team morale in his day.
body: Hearing about Tottenham 's team-bonding trip to Marbella last week made me think about the similar methods I used as a manager to build team morale.
While some things have changed from my day, the idea behind taking your players away to a new environment where they will benefit from spending a lot of time together has not.
I wrote a few weeks ago about how Spurs boss Roberto de Zerbi needed time with his players on the training pitch after their poor start to the season, to bed them in and build a proper team.
He will have used their warm-weather camp in southern Spain to do more of that, getting to know what is almost a new squad of players.

articles.title: Kawhi Leonard: a hero’s complicated return to the Toronto Raptors
articles.summary: The reunion between one of the best players of his generation and the team he helped make an NBA champion is an opportunity to change narratives. When Kawhi Leonard became a Toronto Raptor for the first time in the summer of 2018, he looked shellshocked.
body: “The narrative of not wanting to come to this city is gone,” the team’s president, Masai Ujiri, said at that 2018 press conference, speaking to insecure Raptors fans who had watched American players like Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, and Chris Bosh leave Toronto since the franchise opened its doors in 1995. “We should move past that. Believe in this city. Believe in yourselves … We are proud of who we are.”

But even a historic season wasn’t enough to convince Leonard to stay north of the border. After a long and contentious free-agency period managed by his uncle, Dennis Robertson, Leonard spurned the reigning champions in favor of his hometown Los Angeles Clippers. “There wasn’t as much anger in 2019 as there was with Vince Carter or some of the other guys who left,” says Bruce Arthur, who has covered Leonard since 2018 for the Toronto Star. “I think he was given a little bit of special dispensation because he was going home, because he had delivered a title, and because I never felt like there was ever a connection outside of Kawhi the basketball player, with Toronto.”

articles.title: 'Not in our DNA' - will 3v3 change the future of English football?
articles.summary: Changes have been implemented by the FA from this season with under-7s dropping from playing 5v5 to 3v3 in England - could it help to change the DNA of English football?
body: Shortly after England's disappointing defeat by Argentina at this summer's World Cup, boss Thomas Tuchel offered his view on why the Three Lions are struggling to win major tournaments.
"It's maybe not in our DNA like it is in the Spanish DNA or Argentinian or Brazilian DNA to take the ball, control the game and the ball, which is also a big problem."
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid), in scientific terms, usually refers to the master blueprint for life - the hereditary material in humans and almost all other organisms.
In football, the DNA of a team starts out at grassroots level, where young players are shaped and developed.

articles.title: Bournemouth vs Sunderland: What Has Been Said Following The Game
articles.summary: Bournemouth vs Sunderland was played on Sunday afternoon, just a few short days after they had both won in the Europa League. Both teams went into this game desperate for a league win that would take them out of the bottom three, and when the game began, it appeared that only one team wanted the …
body: The game ended 2-0 to Bournemouth; however, it could have been more. Here is what has been said since the final whistle from the managers, players, pundits, and the fans.

Sunderland’s head coach said: “We were below the level today. It is hard to take – it is really painful. We were not Sunderland today and that is not acceptable. “I am disappointed for our fans because they were with us until the end, but we were not there on the pitch, which is a big problem in the Premier League.”

Co-Commentator on the game, Rob Green, said after the game, “It was a gift, wasn’t it? Something that was a comfortable afternoon and one in the Premier League, you don’t expect to come around too often. The goals that was given to them and the red card that was awarded, Sunderland were the masters of their own downfall really. It should have been more from Bournemouth, it’s a big win for them.”

Bournemouth’s head coach said: “If I’m honest, I feel relief, but not just me. That’s what I feel, everyone here in the club, because everyone feels that the work we do is good, that the way we stick together is good.

articles.title: Gluckstadt set to open new $10 million sports venue
articles.summary: Gluckstadt is now less than two months away from welcoming its first multimillion-dollar sports venue. The TD Select Baseball facility appears to be opening within six weeks, with the state-of-the-art $10 million baseball and soccer complex at 589 Stout Road set to be finished by late November.
body: Both TD Select owner Ty Dean and commercial estate developer Lee Sahler confirmed the November timeline after installing and watering the grass at the venue’s outdoor baseball fields.
“The grass is down already and now we’re just looking to get the lights and fence up so weather permitting we should be open within six weeks,” Sahler told the Clarion Ledger.
Conceptualized as a youth development complex, TD Select Baseball will feature a 10,000-square-foot training indoor facility equipped with 10 batting cages.
The 40-acre complex also has four outdoor baseball fields and a pair of soccer pitches to facilitate youth games and travel tournaments.

articles.title: Definitive proof that Liverpool's transfer strategy is working
articles.summary: Liverpool have developed a reputation for having one of the best academies in world football in recent years. The club has the ability to show prospective additions a clear pathway to the first-team, and the Reds’ senior squad has been littered with academy graduates in recent years.
body: Trent Alexander-Arnold, Curtis Jones, Harvey Elliott, Conor Bradley, Jarell Quansah and Coaimhin Kelleher are just some of the examples of recent graduates from the Kirkby to have become important parts of the team at Anfield.
The club have adopted the strategy of recruiting some of the world’s most promising youngsters to the academy, and it is clearly working.
Lewis Koumas, Trey Nyoni and Rio Ngumoha have all established themselves as important first-team squad players in the early days of Andoni Iraola’s tenure at Anfield.
Koumas is a true academy product, having signed for the Reds at u11 level, but Nyoni and Ngumoha were both signed aged 16.

articles.title: US GP talking points: How will Hamilton, Norris move on from woes?
articles.summary: Formula 1 returns to Austin's Circuit of The Americas for the United States Grand Prix with a historic championship crowning potentially in the offing, along with several other hot topics on the agenda.
body: The event in Texas kicks off the second of three triple-headers to end the season, with races in Mexico and Brazil immediately following this one.
There is every chance that Antonelli will become F1's youngest ever world champion on one of the next three Sundays, but it would require something quite dramatic for that to be in Austin.
Antonelli would need to win the United States Grand Prix and for his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to finish ninth or lower, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton also finishing fifth or lower.
However the weekend plays out, it will be fascinating to see how Antonelli handles the pressure of the title being attainable for the first time.

articles.title: Carrick is handling Shea Lacey all wrong and it could force a bitter departure
articles.summary: Many cannot understand why Shea Lacey has not featured in the last four Manchester United games. The last time the academy graduate played, he produced an eye-opening performance against Leeds.
body: United may have lost that game and been knocked out of the Carabao Cup, but Lacey’s performance, crowned by a beauty of a goal, should have strengthened his case for starts and more minutes. Instead, Michael Carrick has rewarded that display by gluing him to the bench.

That has been baffling. In every game since, United have been crying out for a goal, a spark, or something different from the bench. Yet Carrick has ignored him while the team struggles to score, managing only three goals despite creating plenty of chances.

One of JJ Gabriel’s biggest concerns, and his reason for wanting out, is that he is not being guaranteed the game time he believes he deserves. Would the Lacey treatment give him, or any other academy star, hope of a key role under Carrick?
Even Harry Amass, who used to fill in at left-back under Ruben Amorim and did a decent job, is being overlooked, despite Carrick having no natural left-back.

articles.title: What next for Kartal after 'unbelievable week' in Wuhan
articles.summary: Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets.
body: Kartal became just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to play in a WTA 1000 final with superb wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini, world No 6 Elina Svitolina and former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko.

It is arguably the most impressive tournament performance from a British female player since Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open, particularly given Kartal only returned to action last month following six months out due to a stress fracture in her back.
"We have had an unbelievable week. Not many people expected me to be here and bring these levels," said the 24-year-old after losing 2-6 6-4 6-2 to this year's French Open runner-up Chwalinska.
"I hope I can be in many more of these finals. It was not the result I wanted today but those people in my box are the reason I am healthy, I am here and why I am back to fitness."
